display.purpose: Landing headlines. Fluid: clamp(2.75rem, 1.5rem + 5.4vw, 5.25rem); the frontmatter holds the maximum. Class .t-display.

name.purpose: A person's name at the top of their page: the largest thing in the app. Fluid: clamp(2.5rem, 1.6rem + 4vw, 4.75rem). Class .t-name.

control.purpose: Text inside fields and buttons. 16px so iOS does not zoom on focus; 500 in fields, 600 in buttons, 700 on the primary button.

label.purpose: Field labels, navbar items and small panel headings, in sentence case. Class .t-label (coloured text-2).

chip.purpose: Text inside a chip on a person's card. The one size below 15px, and only inside a pill.

code.purpose: Code inside chat markdown only. The system monospace stack, never used for interface text.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--ease-out-soft, EASE_OUT, and Tailwind's ease-out). Entrances decelerate; nothing overshoots.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: State changes: a field's edge, a card's hover lift (--dur).

motion.name: dur-press
motion.purpose: Button fill and press feedback (scale to 0.97).

motion.name: enter
motion.purpose: The standard entrance: fade up a few pixels. Siblings stagger by 40ms, capped at one screenful.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Physical feedback such as layout shifts and chips entering. Critically damped, so it settles without bounce.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Looping animation stops and travel is removed; state changes still happen. Framer Motion follows it through MotionConfig.

narrative.overview:
Nexia is a slambook: one person keeping track of the people they care about. There are no photos in it, so a person's identity on screen is a colour and a shape. Everything else stays out of the way: a white page, flat pastel surfaces with large corners, one friendly typeface, and one colour that means "do this".

The personality is cute and polished. Cute comes from the shapes, the pastels and the round corners. Polished comes from restraint: flat fills, a single type family, generous space, and no decoration that isn't carrying information.
keyCharacteristics: A white page. Colour belongs to people, not to the chrome.

Each person has one of six colours and one of seven shapes, derived from their profile id (`features/profiles/identity.ts`). A person looks the same in the grid, on their page, in a dialog and in a chat result.
One family, Alan Sans. Hierarchy is size and weight.
Fields are white, defined by their edge.
No native browser UI: no `<select>`, date input, `alert()`, `confirm()` or `title` tooltip.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on a colour use that colour's `-ink`. The base, `-soft` and `-tint` steps are surfaces, never foregrounds.

rules.name: The Person Rule
rules.body: Colour on a signed-in screen means a person. Do not use a person colour as decoration next to real people. The exceptions are fixed and listed: the logo, the three shapes in an empty state, the count beside "Your people", the four chat suggestions, and the landing page.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: One tangerine button per view. Everything else is neutral (`secondary`), quiet (`ghost`) or, on a person's colour, `frost`.

rules.name: The White Field Rule
rules.body: Fields are white with a 1.5px `--field-line` edge. Never tint a field.

dos: Put a `person-*` class on the outermost element that is about one person, and use the `p` utilities inside it.
Check ink-on-colour contrast when adding a colour: 4.5:1 for text.
Draw the sparse case. Only a name and a relationship are required, and the page has to look finished with just those.
donts: Add a shadow, a blur, a gradient, or a border on a card.
Use a person colour for text, or as decoration on a signed-in screen.
Put a second tangerine button in a view.
Add a label above a heading, or uppercase tracked text.
